Title: Runtime Operations Synthesis and Experiment Manual

Overview

This document codifies a single, operationally-oriented reference that synthesizes runtime architecture intent, kernel-scheduler policy patterns, profiling procedures, benchmark experiment templates, release-note instrumentation requirements, common triage matrices for known issues, and runbook steps for critical runtime incidents. The target audience is SREs, runtime engineers, and applied ML engineers running end-to-end performance experiments and rollouts. This is intentionally cross-cutting: use it when designing experiments that touch serving, scheduling, telemetry, and model rollout safety.

Scope

- Cross-layer guidance for runtime architecture and scheduling decisions
- Profiling playbook for reproducible micro- and macro-benchmarks
- A canonical benchmarking experiment matrix and CLI examples
- Release note checklist specific to kernel/scheduler/quantization changes
- Known-issues triage matrix and emergency runbooks
- Links to team wiki pages and owners for deeper dives

1. Architecture intent summary

- Goal: Keep 99th-percentile token-latency predictable for mixed short/long request surfaces while minimizing per-token cost and preserving model fidelity.
- Execution model: hierarchical execution cohorts -> kernel pipeline -> device-level executor -> KV-cache layer -> network ingress.
- Decision contracts:
  - Scheduler must expose: priority, preemption_policy, batch_shaping_hint, affinity_hint.
  - Runtime must preserve KV-cache continuity across model swaps or shard remapping with no user-visible token duplication.

Diagram (textual)

[diagram]
Node: Frontend router (route/policy) -> Admission controller (SLO gating) -> Scheduler (cohort classification) -> Kernel dispatcher -> GPU executor (per-device) -> KV cache store -> Response aggregator
[/diagram]

2. Scheduler policy grammar (reference)

- Policies are declared as YAML fragments in experiments and ingested by the scheduler-reconciler. Example:

```yaml
name: slo-tiered-fastpath
priority: high
preemption_policy: best-effort
batch_shaping_hint:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  preferred_sequence_length: [8, 64, 512]
affinity_hint:
  allow_cross_gpu: true
  numa_preference: node-local
```

- Notes:
  - priority: low|normal|high|critical
  - preemption_policy: none|best-effort|aggressive
  - batch_shaping_hint drives kernel-selection heuristics; mismatches create fallback logs under runtime.kernels.fallback

3. Profiling playbook (reproducible experimental protocol)

Objective: produce a causal attribution between observed latency regressions and kernel/scheduler changes with <5% false-positive rate for alerting.

Preconditions:
- Snapshot the serving traffic sample (10k requests representative surface) and pin model_version + quant_profile.
- Reserve a quiet maintenance fleet (min 3 homogeneous GPUs) and enable full tracing for the trace-id range.

Step-by-step:
1. Prepare trace corpus: run shadow-replay against local harness with --preserve-headers --sticky-session.
2. Baseline run (A): run the microbenchmark suite (see CLI below) for 30 minutes, collect kernel latency histograms, occupancy, NVLink errors.
3. Change under test: apply scheduler or kernel patch to canary worker group.
4. Treatment run (B): repeat the microbenchmark with identical seed and traffic replay.
5. Compare: use the profiler diff tool to generate causal attribution report. Look for increases in kernel-tail (>95th) and shifts in batch-size distributions.
6. If >10% regression in 99th latency or >5% drop in throughput, abort rollout and follow rollback runbook.

Profiling CLI examples

- Shadow replay harness (developer machine):
  ./harness/replay --corpus=~/trace-corpus/production-2027-11-07 --target=scheduler-canary --duration=30m

- Microbenchmark command (30m):
  ./bench/run --suite=mixed-short-long --seed=42 --gpu-pool=homogeneous-4

Telemetry to capture (minimum):
- kernel.exec_time_histogram
- scheduler.batch_size_distribution
- kvcache.hits_per_session
- device.occupancy_percentile
- network.rtt_ms

4. Benchmarking suite: canonical experiments

Table: Experiment templates

| name | intent | workload shape | duration | success metric |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| mixed_burst | realistic customer mix | 60% short, 40% long | 60m | 99p latency < 250ms |
| convoys_stress | long-sequence dominated | 100% long | 120m | throughput > baseline * 0.95 |
| small_shortpath | low token per req | 95% < 20 tokens | 30m | median latency < 30ms |

Example orchestration (K8s job YAML snippet for bench-runner):

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: bench-mixed-burst
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: bench-runner
        image: registry/redwood/bench:2028-01
        args: ["--suite=mixed_burst","--duration=60m","--report=/artifacts/report.json"]
      restartPolicy: Never
```

5. Release note and signoff checklist (for runtime/kernel/scheduler changes)

- Summary of change and expected behavioral impact
- Benchmarks: mixed_burst and convoys_stress results attached
- Telemetry dashboards updated: kernel-latency, batch-distribution, cost-per-token
- Rollout plan: canary group size, measurement windows, rollback thresholds
- Owners: runtime-team, scheduler-team, SRE
- Compliance signoffs (if quantization affecting fidelity): applied by research/QA

Release-template (bulleted):
- Change-id: RRT-XXXX
- Authors: <names>
- Canary plan: 5% traffic for 1h -> 20% for 4h -> full
- Abort criteria: 99p latency > +10% OR error-rate increase > 0.1%

6. Known-issues triage matrix (short catalog)

| Issue | Symptoms | Quick mitigation | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| kernel-lockup-on-batch-split | GPU stuck >60s, watchdog alerts | restart process, drain cohort | runtime-oncall | investigating |
| kvcache-eviction-race | elevated cold-start errors when remapping | reduce eviction aggressiveness, force warmup | infra-cache | mitigated |
| scheduler-favors-large-batches | tail latency regressed for short requests | apply temporary cohort mislignment filter | scheduler | triaged |

7. Emergency runbooks

A. Kernel slowdown / tail-latency spike
1. Identify cohort: query runtime.cohort.latency by tag
2. Isolate canary: route 100% of affected traffic to fallback model variant or lower-fidelity quantized model
3. Scale: increase worker count for the cohort (scale-out) for short burst window
4. Collect traces and produce a 'kernel-slowdown' incident package (logs, kernel traces, device counters)
5. If persistent, revert kernel or scheduler change via automated rollback job

B. KV cache corruption detection and recovery
1. Detect: kvcache.error_rate > 0.5% for 5m OR KV checksum mismatch logs
2. Quarantine node: mark node out_of_service in resource manager
3. Warm restart: start a new node and run 'kvcache-warmup --source=peer-healthy --session-window=30m'
4. Rebalance: allow scheduler to rebind sessions once kvcache.hits per session > 0.8

8. Experiment notebook & artifact conventions

- Always include: input corpus id, model_version, quant_profile, scheduler_policy_yaml (attached), machine image hash, and bench-runner report.json
- Artifact layout recommended:
  artifacts/<experiment-id>/{report.json,profiles/*.pb,server-logs/*.log,tooling/compare.html}

9. Team wiki pointers & ownership

- Runtime architecture deep-dive: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/execution-stitching-and-fallback-orchestration-2026
- Scheduler policy language: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-policy-language-declarative-profiles-2026
- Profiling tools and diff runner: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/profiling-playbook/causal-latency-attribution-and-signal-enrichment-playbook-2026

Owners:
- runtime architecture: runtime-platform@redwood.com (Runtime team)
- scheduler policy: scheduler-core@redwood.com
- bench automation: infra-bench@redwood.com

Appendix: Telemetry thresholds (operational)

- SLOs:
  - 99th token latency (hosted API): 250ms - target
  - 95th kernel exec time (device): < 45ms for short-path kernels
  - KV cache hit ratio (hot sessions): > 0.90
- Alert thresholds:
  - latency.99p increased beyond 10% for 15m -> severity P2
  - kernel.exec_time.p99 > 75ms for 5m -> severity P1
